images.filename: Cass Scenic Railroad State Park - Heisler 6 and Shay 11.jpg
images.caption: Cass Scenic Railroad Heisler #6 along with Shay #11 lead a loaded log train down the former C&O mainline. Note the Cass Country store which was built in 1902 in the background and that the locomotives have been temporarily lettered for predecessor logging railroads that operated at Cass. Photo Walter Scriptunas II

images.caption: Pocahontas County, West Virginia, October 1, 2012.:  An original Shay engine #5 transport culverts to a fish passage project in a roadless area on Oats Run in Spruce, WV.  Oats Run is a headwater tributary of Shavers Fork that has native Eastern brook trout.  The culverts are part of a large-scale restoration project  to improve fish passage.  Cass Scenic Railroad is a partner in the project funded by the Eastern Brook Trout Joint Venture. The engine was once used to haul timber from Spruce, once a bustling town, but now abandoned.  Cass Scenic Railroad will haul all materials and heavy equipment via the rail line. Credit: Keith McGilvray/USFWS.
images.alt: Pocahontas County, West Virginia, October 1, 2012.:  An original Shay engine #5 transport culverts to a fish passage project in a roadless area on Oats Run in Spruce, WV.
